_what: Recorded equivalences between setup-key values. A waiver is how a human says 'these two hashes are the same setup, and here is the evidence'. Without one, a hash difference refuses reuse, which is the default and the safe direction.
_scope: A waiver names ONE field. Every other field still has to match exactly, so waiving arm_sha cannot smuggle in a different model, fixture or judge format.

run_suite.py between 361e8ea9 and d9498c1f (Queue A, A8/A11/A12/A13/A15). What changed: summarise() moved to run_report.py and imported back, gaining the recovery/tool-counter columns there (A8; it formats the markdown report and never reads or writes a row's fields beyond displaying them); `import row_extra`, EXTRA cleared before each arm call and copied onto the row as `arm_extra` only when non-empty (A11); monolith_test_arm, author_workflow and author_judge_workflow added to the arm registration loops (A11-A13; they register new arm names and leave existing entries in ARMS as they were); _eval_params calls processor.adapter_fingerprint(arm_name) instead of adapter_fingerprint() (A11); the inline waivers.json read replaced by setup_key.load_waivers() and a --waivers ID option (A15); an unused `defaultdict` import removed. Why behaviour is identical for baseline: adapter_fingerprint(arm) differs from adapter_fingerprint() only for an arm registered in processor.ARM_TOOLS, and ARM_TOOLS is empty for baseline, so the keyed adapter is unchanged; nothing baseline runs writes row_extra.EXTRA, so it is empty and the row is unchanged; run_task, score() and the arm function itself are untouched. Verified: tools/fingerprint_check.py --baseline 361e8ea9 -> PASS, adapter/recovery/_eval_params identical under tools and markers; prompt_sha 'none' at both revisions. Both hashes computed from the git blobs of the two file versions; the old one equals the arm_sha on this arm's recorded matrix rows. Does NOT cover a model or transport change: ollama_client's transport refactor (A1a) is not in arm_sha and is attested separately by seam_capture.py (48/48 byte-identical).
